title: Mukhtar Washeem v. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited
coram: Sunita Agarwal, J.; Vipin Chandra Dixit, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; relegated to Section 127 appeal.
headnote: Writ challenging an assessing authority's demand computation and disconnection, including a plea that recovery was barred by Section 56(2) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, dismissed. The Division Bench held that those arguments could be raised in a statutory appeal under Section 127, which was the appropriate remedy.
facts: The petitioner, Mukhtar Washeem, approached the Allahabad High Court against Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited, challenging a demand notice as illegally computed and the order disconnecting his electricity. He argued that the respondents could not realise electricity dues after the period stipulated in Section 56(2) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The dispute was treated as a challenge to computation by the assessing authority.

holding_units.holding: A writ challenging computation of a demand by the assessing authority, and disconnection in realisation of that demand, is not maintainable. The consumer has a statutory appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003; contentions that recovery is barred by Section 56(2) read with Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, may be urged before that appellate forum.

principle_tags.application: The demand was treated as computation by the assessing authority; the writ against that computation and disconnection was dismissed in favour of the Section 127 appeal.
The petitioner was relegated to appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003; the writ was dismissed accordingly.

not_decided.point: Whether Section 56(2) of the Electricity Act, 2003 barred realisation of the demanded dues after the stipulated period.
not_decided.note: The Court said the argument could be made in the Section 127 appeal.

not_decided.point: Whether Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 was breached in raising or recovering the demand.
Merits of the demand computation and the legality of the disconnection order.
